questions.question: What experimental corpus was used to derive the initial subgroup rules for propylene oxidation?

options.A: 120 SiO2-supported three-component catalysts based on Ru, W, and P, tested across 200–400°C
options.B: 746 four- and five-component catalysts tested only at 400°C
options.C: 120 Mo/V oxide catalysts tested for n-butane oxidation
options.D: 90 catalysts supported on alumina and tested from 25–100°C

questions.rationale: The initial HTE set contained 120 Ru/W/P compositions measured over multiple reaction temperatures.
questions.evidence_quote: 120 different three-component catalyst compositions containing ruthenium, tungsten and phosphorus

questions.question: Which reaction output was used as the target variable in the subgroup-discovery analysis?

options.A: Yield of the oxygenates acrolein and acrylic acid from propylene
options.B: Total propylene conversion regardless of products
options.C: Selectivity to CO and CO2 combustion products
options.D: Catalyst lifetime during repeated oxidation cycles

questions.rationale: The subgroup analysis targets oxygenate yield rather than an average global model of all products.

questions.question: Which three descriptors were identified as key for high oxygenate yields in the original three-component Ru/W/P set?

options.A: Temperature, phosphorus content, and composition-weighted electronegativity
options.B: Ru content, catalyst surface area, and pore diameter
options.C: W oxidation state, particle size, and total feed rate
options.D: Temperature, oxygen partial pressure, and support crystallinity

questions.rationale: The abstract and conclusion list these as the key parameters associated with high yield.
questions.evidence_quote: The temperature, the phosphorus content, and the composition-weighted electronegativity are identiﬁed as key parameters

questions.question: What conjunction of thresholds defined the reported high-performance subgroup for the three-component catalysts?

options.A: 280–300°C, phosphorus descriptor >0.55, and weighted electronegativity 3.910–<4.002 eV
options.B: At least 360°C, phosphorus <0.35, and electronegativity >4.10 eV

questions.rationale: The original three-component subgroup rule combines the intermediate temperature interval with P and electronegativity bounds.

questions.question: What subgroup size and quality score were reported when SGD was applied to the combined four-/five-component dataset?
questions.rationale: The selected group was a small exceptional subset of the expanded experimental data.
questions.evidence_quote: The identiﬁed SG presenting the highest m /no (0.355) contains 18 data points

questions.question: Which rules described that high-performing subgroup in the expanded four-/five-component HTE data?

options.A: Temperature ≥360°C, one radius descriptor ≤1.001 Å, and electron affinity <−1.593 eV
options.C: Temperature ≤250°C, Ru>0.35, and radius difference >0.10 Å

questions.rationale: For the larger dataset, the rules shifted to a different set of composition descriptors and a higher temperature.

questions.question: What was the best oxygenate yield reported for a four-component catalyst, and which composition feature was highlighted?

options.A: 60.19% at 400°C for a catalyst with 0.35 Te molar fraction as the added element
options.B: 59.60% at 400°C for a Ta-containing five-component catalyst
options.C: 26.85% at 300°C for the best three-component training catalyst
options.D: 60.19% at 300°C for a catalyst with 0.05 Ru

questions.rationale: The highest four-component yield came from a Te-rich composition at the upper tested temperature.
questions.evidence_quote: highest yield of oxygenates (60.19 % at 400ºC) contains 0.35 molar fraction of tellurium

questions.question: What was the strongest five-component material identified by applying the derived rules, and how did it compare with the three-component training data?

options.A: Ru/W/P/Te/Ta gave 59.60% oxygenate yield at 400°C, more than twice the training-set maximum
options.B: Ru/W/P/Mo/Nb gave 26.85% at 300°C, equal to the training maximum
options.C: Ru/W/P/Te/Ta gave 60.19% at 300°C, only marginally above training
options.D: Ru/W/P/Cr/Sn gave 59.60% at 280°C, below the training maximum

questions.rationale: The conclusion highlights the Te/Ta five-component catalyst as over twice the three-component dataset's top yield.
questions.evidence_quote: a five-component material containing ruthenium, tungsten, phosphorus, tellurium and tantalum

questions.question: Why did the authors warn that the three-component temperature rule did not transfer directly to four-/five-component catalysts?

options.A: Their best oxygenate yields occurred around 400°C, rather than the ~300°C favored in the three-component training set
options.B: The added elements reduced the maximum temperature to 200°C
options.C: The expanded materials were not tested experimentally
options.D: The temperature descriptor was excluded from the expanded SGD analysis

questions.rationale: The authors explicitly note the temperature rule was not transferable because the more complex catalysts peaked at higher temperature.
questions.evidence_quote: The SG rule on the reaction temperature derived based on the three-component materials data set is thus not transferable to the four-component ones.

questions.question: What extrapolation limit did the authors identify for the derived rules when proposing more complex materials?

options.A: They were tested mainly at low Ru loadings and elements with radii compatible with W, so other composition regions may need new training data
options.B: They apply only to catalysts with no phosphorus
options.C: They were derived on five-component materials and cannot guide simpler catalysts
options.D: They require every catalyst to be crystalline rather than disordered

questions.rationale: The paper cautions that exceptional behavior outside the explored Ru/radius domain may require adding new data.
questions.evidence_quote: it is unclear if the SG rules presented in Fig. 5C can identify exceptional materials
